## 4. What was NOT verified

The most useful section of the dossier, and the one the author least wants to write.
Every claim with no command output in section 3 belongs here.

- **Nothing of the prototype exists.** No package, harness, page, install or build was run; every
  "[planned]" and "[assumed]" of `framework_prototype.md` is unmeasured — the review is of the
  plan's design: whether its oracle can actually fail a leaking candidate, whether the page and the
  measures are enough for the Owner to choose, and whether the probes of Evidence ask the right
  questions.
- **Evidence's data path (§3, A1–A6)** is written from my knowledge of Evidence, not read from its
  40.1.8 code. Whether it prerenders query results into HTML, and whether page code can reach its
  DuckDB-WASM instance, is open.
- **`verify` on a foreign output (§2.5).** Not tried. I read `release.verify` and `_package`: it takes
  the one `manifest.json` of the whole folder, and refuses any extension outside the media types and
  any `sourceMappingURL` — which a framework's output may carry in its bundles even with source maps
  off. Whether either candidate's output survives `verify` with a narrow inclusion list is open.
- **Whether `encrypt_package` and `validate_manifest` accept one profile, or a profile with no
  report** — §2.2's fallback. I read `_validate_declaration`, which does not refuse a profile with no
  report, but did not read `validate_manifest` for that case.
- **DuckDB-WASM from jsDelivr in headless Chrome on `127.0.0.1`** — not tried here; M49 ran PBKDF2
  only.
- **M53**: `billingEnabled` false is what the Cloud Billing API returns now; what Google does to a
  Spark project when the account's trial closes is not measured (stated in the row).

## 7. Where I hesitated

Decisions that could have gone the other way, with the reason they went this one.

- **The oracle is the gate's `verify`, not a search of its own** (§2.5, §8): it means a candidate's
  output must already fit the gate's inclusion list and media types — strict, and possibly failing a
  candidate for a reason unrelated to clear data (a `manifest.json` of its own, a
  `sourceMappingURL` comment). I kept it because whatever is chosen must pass that same function in
  2.5. The criterion speaks only of clear data at build time, so §2.5 splits the refusals: by
  content fails the criterion; by form is a cost cleared by a build setting, and fails only if no
  setting clears it. Whether that split leaves a hole — a leak that shows up only as a form
  refusal, and is then "cleared" — is worth a look.
- **Vega-Lite for the own build** (§4): it could equally be ECharts, which makes the charts
  comparable with Evidence's. A choice the Owner may overturn.
- **An invented fixture with P01's real columns** rather than reading the real view: real data
  needs 2.4's source gate; invented values keep "no report data before 2.4".
- **Prototypes tracked in the repository, outside `make check`** (§5): their npm dependencies would
  make the gate slow and network-bound; tracked so the review sees what was measured.
- **The fixed notice for the partial month** instead of deriving it: M5's rule is 2.5's; the
  prototype only needs the page to have the notice somewhere.

## Round 1 — FPROTO

### 1. Conclusion

**Changes required.** One blocking finding, four adjustments and one observation. The proposed
oracle can accept artifacts containing recoverable clear report data, even when its planned
Parquet counter-proof succeeds. The plan therefore cannot yet go to implementation under the
stated acceptance bar. No framework choice is made by this review.

### 2. Reviewed scope and version

- Branch: `main`, initially clean, ahead of `origin/main` by three commits.
- Checkout: `f537ec49cf336bb252348e11d7d694a72fdecb2a`.
- Fixed comparison: `6cdcca4..2178322`, exactly `75209c9` and `2178322`; all nine changed files
  examined. `f537ec4` adds only the author's dossier and is excluded from the delivery review.
- No initial tracked changes or untracked files. This review changes only `DOSSIER.md`.
- Full revision-1 prototype plan reviewed against the specified PLAN criteria, conventions,
  package gate and envelope, tracing `release.verify`, `_package`, `contract.inspect`/`needles`
  and the producer/manifest validation. The existing gate's documented limits are context,
  not findings reopened against stage 2.2b.

### 3. Findings by severity

**FPROTO-1-01 — The oracle can pass clear query results. Verdict: `blocking` (high).**

Location: `docs/framework_prototype.md:109`, `:117`, `:126`, `:151`, `:238`, `:255`.

`verify` is a necessary publishing check, but its success is insufficient for this stage's stronger
claim. `release.py:318` reads files without decoding; `contract.py:354` constructs specific byte
spellings and `:368` searches substrings. The limitations are explicit in `package_gate.md` §6.
Eligible source amounts do not guarantee detection of their serialized or aggregated results:
`1234.50` is searched, whereas a JavaScript number can be `1234.5`; binary numeric Arrow columns
contain neither decimal spelling. Gzip, brotli, base64 and escaped text also evade the search.
Raw HTML, JSON/devalue and JavaScript are seen when they retain a needle; an encoded payload in a
service worker is subject to the same blind spot. Runtime browser CacheStorage is outside this
filesystem inspection entirely.

This is a normal candidate data path, not solely an adversarial construction. The downloaded,
pinned `@evidence-dev/universal-sql@3.0.1`
[`src/cache-duckdb.js`](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@evidence-dev/universal-sql@3.0.1/src/cache-duckdb.js)
lines 63–95 serialize server query results as Arrow IPC into
`.svelte-kit/output/prerendered/dependencies/api/prerendered_queries/<hash>.arrow`.
Evidence 40.1.8's
[`template/src/pages/+layout.js`](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@evidence-dev/evidence@40.1.8/template/src/pages/+layout.js)
lines 62–75 retrieve those caches in the browser. A1 names Parquet/HTML/JSON, omitting this carrier.
The clear-mode Parquet alone can kill the counter-proof while leaving this second path untested.

The form/content split compounds that gap: inclusion/extensions, source maps and multiple manifests
can stop `verify` before value inspection (`release.py:255`, `:264`, `:326`). The executed probes
below confirm that clear content in a second manifest or map receives only a form refusal. Removing
that output in a rebuild can erase the evidence without proving that build-time report queries
stopped. Thus the first refusal cannot determine that the original output was only a form problem.

Evidence: **static source trace and executed end-to-end probes**, transcript in §4. A valid encrypted
package and empty public-values list passed; numeric Arrow, compressed data and encoded payloads
also passed. The same harness rejected raw Parquet and plain-text leaks. No checker was patched.

Correction: retain `verify` unchanged and specify a supplementary prototype inspection/data-path
proof that covers each candidate's actual emitted carriers and query results, including relevant
decoding, or refuses unsupported carriers explicitly. Preserve original outputs and inspect their
content independently of form failures before allowing a setting to clear them. A lack of coverage
must be inconclusive/failing, never a pass. Give each carrier an independent negative control with
no other clear Parquet/value to trip the checker; include candidate-generated Arrow and numeric
serialization, not just the hand-made folder. Demonstrate that a build-time report query cannot
be accepted merely because its output was removed or re-encoded. Keep the fixture-needle coverage
assertion explicit, using `needles`, rather than inferring it from decimal wording.

Validation: the clean encrypted controls pass; every supported clear carrier is independently
rejected; unsupported ones prevent acceptance. A content-plus-form mutant cannot become a claimed
criterion pass through the form workaround. None of this changes the publishing gate's guarantees.

**FPROTO-1-02 — The documented harness layout cannot call `verify` successfully. Verdict:
`adjustment` (medium).**

Location: `docs/framework_prototype.md:62`, `:71`, `:112`.

The plan calls `<candidate>/release/` the verifier root and lists contract, profiles, inclusion list
and media types there. The API appends `release/` itself (`release.py:98`, `contract.py:384`), and
also unconditionally reads `public_values.json`, which the plan never provisions. The common
contract/profiles are described at yet another, shared path. Executing the stated layout fails
before any candidate inspection; that harness failure must not be recorded as a candidate cost.

Evidence: **static and executed**. Passing the documented release directory produced
`FileNotFoundError` for `release/release/profiles.json`; using its parent without the unlisted
public-values file failed on `release/public_values.json` (§4). Supplying the complete parent-root
layout made the diagnostic control pass.

Correction: specify one complete, consistent harness layout and actual `verify(root, output,
live=...)` call. Explain how the shared declarations reach each candidate root, include an empty
fixture public-values declaration, and use the API's `site/`-prefixed inclusion syntax. Reference
the owning gate document for formats. Validate the harness on a clean package and a clear-value
mutation before building either candidate, with infrastructure errors distinguished from refusals.

**FPROTO-1-03 — `order_count` cannot be shown as specified at the summary grain. Verdict:
`adjustment` (medium).**

Location: `docs/framework_prototype.md:63`, `:90`, `:137`.

The fixture's grain is month/channel/category, with two categories per root. The table instead
groups by month/root category, including multiple channels for "todos", but asks for an
`order_count` per displayed row. Several native counts contribute to that row; the view does not
carry order identities from which their union could be computed. Neither summing them nor choosing
one produces the defined metric. Omitting the total row's count does not resolve the detail rows.
Comparing the same erroneous query in Python and the browser would still pass §2.6.

Evidence: **static**, against M4 and the pinned upstream P01 SQL, whose columns and grouping were
independently fetched through GitHub. The shape probe in §4 has up to six native rows per displayed
cell, or two after filtering one channel.

Correction: define where the native counts are displayed — for example, a detail table at the
contract grain — and leave counts unavailable in summaries that cannot preserve that grain.
Validate a fixture with overlapping category populations and unequal native counts; assert the
native values and absence of a fabricated summary count independently of the rendering query.

**FPROTO-1-04 — The fixture does not guarantee the promised empty-slice exercise. Verdict:
`adjustment` (medium).**

Location: `docs/framework_prototype.md:51`, `:53`, `:88`, `:93`, `:139`.

Removing one channel/category/month row leaves its sibling category in the same displayed
month/root-category group. The only filter is a channel selected from existing data: it cannot
select that absent native combination, and every channel still has other rows. Fewer rows in the
last month also need not empty any displayed group. Consequently a fixture conforming to those
shape rules can exercise no empty cell at all; the browser script has no specified action or
expected location for "the empty slice".

Evidence: **static plus executed fixture-shape counterexample** (§4): 224 rows, the requested native
gap and nine last-month rows, yet all 39 month/root-category cells exist under every channel filter.
This checks the dimensional shape, not an implementation of the unbuilt full fixture.

Correction: make a named gap at the page's displayed grain, or specify controls/detail rows that
reach the native gap. Pin the exact selection, missing cell and expected Portuguese notice for
both candidates. Validate that the browser reaches that case and distinguishes absence from zero;
a mutation that fills the gap or suppresses the notice must fail that check.

**FPROTO-1-05 — Performance results have no fixed cache/delivery protocol. Verdict:
`adjustment` (medium).**

Location: `docs/framework_prototype.md:134`, `:143`, `:214`, `:215`, `:229`.

The reference to M49 supplies a headless-browser mechanism, but does not specify cache reset and
reuse between candidates, clear/encrypted builds or the five logins. A first cold engine fetch and
four warm logins can be combined into a median without identifying those conditions. Moreover,
Evidence's pinned browser module bundles local WASM/worker URLs, while B uses jsDelivr; a local
static server and the CDN need not use the same HTTP compression or cache behavior. The resulting
bytes/times could reflect prior cache state and serving choices rather than a reproducible
comparison. No biased result is claimed to have been measured yet.

Evidence: **static protocol gap**. `universal-sql@3.0.1/src/client-duckdb/browser.js:40` imports WASM
and workers through Vite; the plan explicitly chooses CDN loading for B. The existing network
allowlist does include the CDN, so exclusion of CDN requests is not alleged.

Correction and validation: specify fresh profiles/storage for cold runs, separately labelled warm
runs, identical timer boundaries, and recorded HTTP compression/cache conditions. Define wire-byte
accounting across all requests, including workers/WASM/CDN, with an origin breakdown so Firebase
transfer and total transfer remain distinguishable. Preserve request/cache flags and conditions
with the results; do not combine cold and warm samples into an unexplained five-run statistic.

**FPROTO-1-06 — `env -i` is not a dependency-execution sandbox. Verdict: `observation` (low).**

Location: `docs/framework_prototype.md:168`, `:195`, `:197`, `:227`.

Ordinary `npm ci` may run dependency lifecycle scripts before A6, which is last. Retaining the
Owner's `HOME` leaves credential files/configuration discoverable; environment scrubbing also
does not remove filesystem access to the checkout or host publishing tools. An exact lockfile
does not restrict that execution. The fake-HOME demonstration in §4 confirms the filesystem point
without reading an actual credential. No malicious dependency or attempted publication was found:
the exploitation scenario is adversarial, hence an observation under this review's severity rule.

Recommendation: move script assessment before the first install, start with `--ignore-scripts`,
and record any required hooks. If host credentials/publishing paths must be inaccessible, run
hooks and builds in a disposable environment without those files or writable publishing checkout;
a throwaway `HOME` alone is not a filesystem sandbox. Otherwise record the residual supply-chain
risk explicitly in §5. Validate any claimed isolation with fake credential and publishing-path
sentinels, not real credentials.

## Round 1 — the author's answer

Revision 2 of `docs/framework_prototype.md` answers all six findings; each Status above says where.
It is still a plan: nothing of the prototype is built, and every **[planned]** and **[assumed]** in it
is unmeasured. Two things were run for it, on 2026-11-20:

The pin it cites. P01's model at `mvp_eng_dados_2` `b0ef66e` (N91) has the same twelve columns, in
the same order, as at `f86b9fb` — read with `git show b0ef66e:dbt/models/consumption/monthly_revenue_by_channel_and_category.sql`
in that checkout; the plan cites M59 for it, and links nothing of `mvp_eng_dados_2` before N86.

The sandbox premise of §5, unprivileged, with the home folder not bound:

```text
$ bwrap --version
bubblewrap 0.6.1
$ bwrap --ro-bind /usr /usr --symlink usr/bin /bin --symlink usr/lib /lib --symlink usr/lib64 /lib64 --tmpfs /home --unshare-net --proc /proc --dev /dev /bin/sh -c 'ls /home; test -e /home/doug && echo HOME_VISIBLE || echo home_absent; echo ok'

```

`make check` at the revision: exit 0 (157 JS tests, 156 pass, 1 skipped; Python, docs and ADR
checks green).

**Not verified, and where I hesitated:**

- The differential's premise that both builds are deterministic enough (§9): if Evidence's noise
  covers its bundles, the differential degrades to the inspection there, and the result is
  inconclusive. Not measured.
- The draw against the decoy outputs (§2.1) converging with three-digit integers against Evidence's
  34 MB WASM: not measured. I chose drawing over declaring public values, so that the gate's
  `public_values.json` keeps meaning "public by design".
- The inspection's decoders are a closed list I chose; the differential, not the list, is the
  coverage argument for build output. For the browser (§2.5.3), the inspection alone judges: a
  carrier outside its list there is inconclusive only if it is a binary no layer decodes — a
  re-spelled text value in storage it does not know is the gap I see, bounded by the needles
  including the page's query results.
- `bubblewrap` over Docker: Docker is installed, but its daemon is root; a mount mistake there is
  worse than one in `bwrap`, which binds only what is named.

## Round 2 — FPROTO

### 1. Conclusion

**Changes required.** Three blockers remain. The build oracle can accept a clear query result that
is invariant across fixture seeds, the logout check can miss registered clear Parquet, and the fixed
fixture shape can cause an honest build to fail the gate. Stage 2.3's plan review stays open.

### 2. Reviewed scope and version

- `main` at `da75364f5e9eac79d4588d2e06a3097ce19086ed`, four commits ahead of `origin/main`.
  The working tree started clean with zero untracked files. HEAD stayed at that revision during
  the review. The report is the sole working-tree change.
- Compared `docs/framework_prototype.md` at `2178322` (revision 1) and `2542943` (revision 2) using
  the supplied path-restricted diff. Reviewed only the six Status edits and the author's answer in
  `da75364`. Intervening pin and Owner-decision commits supplied context where relevant.
- Applied `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, PLAN §3.4, §6.2 stage 2.3 and §7, and the owning gate and
  envelope documents. Traced the current verifier, the contract filters and the relevant pinned
  Evidence and SvelteKit paths. The framework choice remains the Owner's.

### 3. Findings by severity

#### High — blocking

**FPROTO-2-01 — The differential can pass a build that queried clear data.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:195–234`, `:473–477`, `PLAN.md:61`.

N22 puts the password below the login box, and the staged build receives the sealed package and the
reader. An ordinary shared login/demo helper can supply the public password to prerender code, even
if the wrapper provides no password variable or file. The successful extraction of a result also
need not change any delivered bytes. A query can emit a stable dimension or count from the fixed
shape, or its result can be discarded before output. A path with a varying build stamp is already
in X/X noise, so Y's differences at that path can be ignored. The inspector further excuses
undecoded binaries on X/Y equality, and the differential skips the entire package directory.

The synthetic diagnostic decrypted two different fixtures using the same public test input, queried
`min(month_number)`, and wrote `export const firstMonth = 11;`. All three calls to the real `verify`
passed and all result bytes were equal. This is a native fixture integer below the gate's threshold,
and §2.5.2 compares integers only in structured carriers. In the full fixture, 13 consecutive
months always give `min(month_number) = 1`, even if X and Y use different windows. The diagnostic
exercised the verifier and query logic, with the pass of the proposed combined rules inferred from
the plan. Evidence's pinned `+layout.js:118–149` supplies a prerender query path and
`cache-duckdb.js:72–96` can serialize its results to Arrow. Candidate execution remains pending.

Keep the sealed package and clear source, including generated sources and query caches, outside the
encrypted-route build. Insert the exact verified package in a trusted post-build step and inspect
both the archived builder output and the complete served artifact. Where a candidate requires a
different arrangement, require direct evidence that its build cannot open the report or execute a
clear-data query. Use X/X/Y as a diagnostic and require evidence for noisy and unknown regions.
Restrict package exemptions to validated envelope bytes. Exercise an invariant result, a noisy
file with a leak and a build-time query whose result is discarded. The underlying gap is preexisting.
Revision 2 introduces the unsound differential and sandbox coverage claims.

**FPROTO-2-02 — The browser oracle misses decrypted bytes in live worker state.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:115–117`, `:259–280`, `:287–302`.

Dropping the SQL table and removing its DOM can both succeed while the DuckDB worker's registered
Parquet and JavaScript's chart/query objects remain reachable. This can happen during ordinary
logout cleanup without writing any of the enumerated storage APIs or making another network
request. A follow-up query against the registered file can still read P01. Evidence's pinned
`src/client-duckdb/browser.js:12–19`, `:53–70` keeps a module-scoped database and worker with a
window reference, and `:98–102` drops registered files separately. DuckDB-WASM 1.32.0's
`async_bindings.d.ts:48–126` declares separate file registration, lookup and removal operations.
This is static evidence of a supported carrier and a missing test, with no browser run.

Account for the live document, hydration data, worker and application state as well as origin
storage. Require proof that each clear-data holder is retired or disposed of at logout. Check for
registered files and retained results, or prove the isolated data-owning context is gone. Account
for response capture from worker and frame targets and treat missing bodies or unsupported used
carriers as inconclusive. Add single-carrier browser controls, including a logout that drops the
table but leaves a registered file. The cleanup blind spot is preexisting. Revision 2 adds useful
storage inspection, with the central runtime carrier still uncovered.

**FPROTO-2-03 — The decoy draw can falsely disqualify Evidence.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:69–98`, `:238–240`, `:485–488`,
`src/bi_como_codigo/contract.py:314–321`, `:354–376`.

The gate inspects the totals' row count, complete totals object and additive sums along with cell
values. The row count is always `226`. The DuckDB 1.32.0 EH WASM previously observed in round 1
contains that byte sequence 33 times, and the actual `contract.inspect` refuses the engine with
`226` as its only eligible value. Evidence's dependency range permits this version and its pinned
browser module imports the EH asset. If the finished output contains these bytes, a correct package
with this shape trips the unchanged gate. Range widening can never redraw `226`. The fixture lock
and candidate build have yet to run, so the measured collision applies to the identified asset.

The draw relies on fixture independence, the property the differential fails to prove.
Calibrating against arbitrary decoy emissions can train the fixture away from actual leaks, while
new bundle noise or a changed hash/build setting can introduce collisions after calibration. Check
the full real `needles` set, including fixed values and derived totals, against a baseline whose
provenance excludes the fixture, and bound the draw. Resolve invariant collisions by revising the
test shape or returning a harness limitation with evidence. Keep gate refusals visible and preserve
`verify` and the meaning of `public_values.json`. Validate with the measured `226` collision and a
true leak in a fixture-aware run. Raw substring collisions are preexisting. The fixed count and the
purported decoy remedy are introduced by revision 2.

#### Medium — adjustment

**FPROTO-2-04 — The verdict and its controls leave ordinary branches undefined.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:179–188`, `:223–283`, `:443–446`.

The new root layout and API call work. The probe also shows that a malformed trusted
`public_values.json` produces `release.Refused(public_values_invalid)`, so classifying every
`Refused` as the candidate's result misattributes a harness defect. The verdict leaves other real
outcomes such as an invalid manifest, corrupt envelope or reserved Hosting path outside its listed
classes. The carrier rules also need an explicit clean path for the validated `.bice` bytes, which
legitimately differ between X and Y and fit none of the listed decoders. Independent inspection and
archival protect a known content failure behind a form refusal, and a known earlier failure stands.
Specify what happens when an earlier archived run was inconclusive and a later setting removes the
carrier. An unresolved earlier run must prevent acceptance.

The label control expects an X/Y difference even though the specified fixture labels are fixed.
The browser control plants two leaks in one run. The natural clear build may exercise several
carriers at once, which can establish discovery. To establish independent detection, isolate each
carrier and assert its local diagnosis even if the gate trips elsewhere. The Arrow cache is
explicitly candidate-native. The other synthetic controls cover their encodings, while A1 must
supply actual carrier samples, including SvelteKit 2.8.4's `serialize_data.js:61–78` JSON-in-HTML
with `data-sveltekit-fetched` and optional `data-b64`, if present in A1 output.

Specify a total verdict and test valid envelopes, malformed trusted declarations, invalid candidate
packages, content plus form, unknown carriers and archived inconclusive results. Use fixed-label
and varying-value controls with the appropriate layer expectations. The incomplete categorization
predates revision 2. The package-inspector ambiguity, blanket trusted-declaration classification
and contradictory control expectations are new.

**FPROTO-2-05 — The amount generator cannot satisfy Z as written.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:58–80`, `:295–307`.

Z requires two `0.00` net amounts and each row's gross to equal its discount. The blanket
distinctness rule across all amounts prohibits both equalities and the duplicate zero, and zero
cannot have three significant digits. A literal generator can reject every draw or lose the case
that distinguishes zero from absence. The dimensional probe confirms 13 months, 226 rows, no G
rows, two Z rows and 12 rows in the final month. The contradiction follows from the amount rules.

State the exact Z exceptions for uniqueness and significance, and count unique needles using
`contract.needles`' deduplication. Check G and Z before sealing and assert both DOM mutations fail.
Keep the count-sum assertion on populated summary groups and independently check the native detail
counts. Revision 2 introduces the contradictory requirements.

**FPROTO-2-06 — The performance protocol leaves pre-submit work and warm state uncontrolled.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:314–332`, `:433–434`, `:452`.

Fresh cold profiles and separate origin totals are specified. The protocol also says cold is
navigation to table, while the reported login timer starts at submit, with no fixed submit trigger
or separate navigation-to-table time in §6. Evidence starts `profile(loadDB)` when `+layout.js`
evaluates (`:20–53`), so an unspecified pause after the login box appears can move engine work
outside the timed interval. Reusing a profile across warm reloads retains origin state as well as
HTTP cache. The stated prime could stop before the encrypted package and engine are fetched. These
are static protocol gaps. No timing or transfer measurement was taken in this review.

Fix the automation trigger for submit, record navigation-to-summary and submit-to-summary as
separate observations, and define a complete priming journey and which state carries over. Collect
worker and page requests under a shared accounting rule that defines how in-flight responses at
each cutoff are counted. Validate with timestamps and request/cache traces for both candidates.
The timing and cache ambiguity is preexisting. Revision 2 narrows it and introduces the conflicting
cold boundaries.

**FPROTO-2-07 — The Status edits are outside the rendered table.**
`DOSSIER.md:158–165` at `da75364`.

The inserted `|| Applied` creates an empty fifth cell and a sixth cell containing each answer. A
five-column GFM table ignores the extra cell. The source diff confirms the extra delimiter in all
six rows. The underlying claims are visible in Markdown source. Put each answer in the fifth cell
and verify the column count and rendered Status. This is a regression in `da75364`.

#### Low — observation

**FPROTO-2-08 — The sandbox probe can miss inherited authority.**

evade the proposed rule for failed attachment.

[Chrome DevTools Target protocol](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Target/#method-setAutoAttach).

## Round 4 — the author's answer

Revision 5 of `docs/framework_prototype.md` answers all seven findings; each Status above says where.
The Owner decided two things on round 4 (PLAN §1.2, N95): the oracle guards against the **ordinary
behaviour** of each candidate — its framework, libraries and browser — and the page code this
repository writes, which you review; code of ours written to deceive the oracle, and a compromised
dependency, are residual risks written in §9 of the plan. And the review goes on until no blocking
finding is left. Please weigh the findings of round 5 against that scope: a case that needs our own
page code to act against the oracle is an observation, not a blocker.

The main changes: no package code runs with a network at all — the harness fetches the tarballs and
every install and build is offline —; numbers are compared by the role of the file, and the draw
calibrates both inspections; store writes are observed as they happen; the package is bound to the
drawn fixture and recognised by digest in the artifact and in the browser. It is still a plan:
nothing of the prototype is built, and every **[planned]** and **[assumed]** is unmeasured.

Run for it: `make check` at each commit, exit 0. Nothing of the candidates was run.

**Not verified, and where I hesitated:**

- That Evidence 40.1.8 installs offline from a fetched cache, with no post-install download of its
  own — A6 now asks it. If it cannot, the result says so.
- Wrapping the stores' write paths in every realm is ordinary instrumentation, but whether the
  DevTools protocol lets it be installed in every worker type before its first script is not
  measured; a realm without it is inconclusive.
- The role split for numbers trusts the classification of a file as code-bearing; a JSON document
  served as code is still parsed as a structured carrier, so its numbers are compared.

### 3. Findings by severity

#### High — blocking

**FPROTO-5-01 — A wrong password triggers `PREMATURE_DECRYPT`.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:406–412,514–520`, `web/envelope.mjs:307–322,350–367`,
`tests/js/envelope.test.mjs:57–89`.

The journey submits a wrong password first. PBKDF2 successfully derives an AES-KW key for that
attempt. The unchanged reader rejects the password at `unwrapKey`, before decrypting the report.
The successful derivation precedes the correct password's `submit`, so the plan marks it as
`PREMATURE_DECRYPT` and permanently fails an otherwise correct candidate. The reader sequence is
static evidence, and the existing wrong-password vectors passed in the review's `make check`.

Define the expected operations per submission. Before any submission, neither a key derivation nor
a report open may start. The wrong attempt may derive a key and fail the unwrap, with no successful
unwrap, report decryption or opened report. Exercise the normal wrong-then-right journey and a
separate startup-decryption control. The wrong-password UI predates revision 2. The conflicting
timing rule and required wrong-password journey appear together in revision 5.

**FPROTO-5-02 — Transient storage writes and history state can escape capture.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:413–438,504`.

The listed `Storage.setItem` hook misses the native named-property setter. SvelteKit 2.8.4 itself
writes `sessionStorage[key]` in `session-storage.js:20–26` and persists component snapshots on
unload or when hidden (`client.js:351–371,2013–2046`). A snapshot of a report filter can contain a
fixture label. If logout cleanup removes it before the snapshots the plan takes, both the hook and
enumeration can miss the write. Updating a cached value through `IDBCursor.update` has the same
gap in the listed IndexedDB hooks. These are ordinary storage paths. Static evidence from the
pinned archive and the API definitions. [SvelteKit storage](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@sveltejs/kit@2.8.4/src/runtime/client/session-storage.js), [SvelteKit client](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@sveltejs/kit@2.8.4/src/runtime/client/client.js), [Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#the-storage-interface), [IndexedDB cursor](https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#dom-idbcursor-update).

The one-entry check proves the final history shape. A normal SvelteKit `replaceState` can put a
report selection into serialized navigation state during the session while keeping one entry.
The full logout navigation can replace that entry before it is checked. `Page.getNavigationHistory`
has no field for serialized state. Observe history state and URLs when written, as well as the
existing Back assertion. Cover the native store mutations through protocol events or equivalent
hooks. Single-carrier controls should assert the mutation or history diagnosis before cleanup,
including a named-property write, a cursor update and a same-entry history update. Separately prove
the collectors for retained values. Context reconciliation and per-key snapshots do not substitute
for those controls. The lifecycle gap predates revision 2. Revision 5 adds the incomplete hooks.
[SvelteKit client `replaceState`](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@sveltejs/kit@2.8.4/src/runtime/client/client.js), [HTML History API](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#dom-history-replacestate), [CDP Page domain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-protocol/master/pdl/domains/Page.pdl), [CDP DOMStorage events](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-protocol/master/pdl/domains/DOMStorage.pdl).

**FPROTO-5-03 — The clean metadata and bundle control contradicts the predicates.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:84–90,139–150,361–382,490`,
`src/bi_como_codigo/contract.py:328–376`.

The clean control adds a JSON document with protocol version `1` and a month number. A JSON
document found anywhere is data-bearing, and its integers are compared as values. Every permitted
61-month fixture contains month numbers 1–12. The scratch diagnostic confirmed the intersection
for all starting months and confirmed that the existing gate's small-integer rule accepts this
metadata. If the draw applies the supplemental predicate to that JSON in the builder output, it
cannot converge. If the draw skips the JSON, the later inspection can fail the clean artifact.
The other half of the control specifies that an incidental shortest-JavaScript literal matches the
fixture amount even though it was present during calibration. A proper draw rejects that pairing.

Specify the metadata fields whose schema and provenance establish their meaning and keep the rest
of those documents searchable. Use identical recursive role dispatch in the draw and the scan.
Require the metadata control to pass with a separate report-data integer control that fails, and
require the incidental literal to reject a draw before the accepted fixture clears it. The gap
between gate and supplemental eligibility dates to revision 2. These conflicting role rules and
the clean control are new in revision 5.

**FPROTO-5-04 — An earlier missing mandatory observation can disappear from the verdict.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:448–477,494–505`.

The absent-stage and interrupted-capture branches apply only to the latest run. Suppose artifact A
passes assembly, `verify` and static inspection, but browser capture never starts. No file, target,
context, body or store was marked inconclusive because no capture exists. A different artifact B
then completes cleanly. The written precedence permits `passes` even though A had no browser
observation and B has a different digest. The existing table tests an absent stage on the latest
run and a later pass after an explicitly inconclusive object. It omits this sequence. This follows
from the specified branches without running the harness.

Define the mandatory stages for each terminal outcome of a judged run. An assembly `FORM` can
legitimately make `verify` and browser capture inapplicable, while its archived builder output
still requires inspection. Keep a missing required observation on an earlier judged artifact open
under the equivalent-state retry rule. Make probe and control runs explicit in the inputs to the
verdict. Prove both `assembly FORM` with its required inspection and `capture absent on A → pass
on B`, plus successful resolution on A. Revision 2 introduced archive-aware precedence.
Revision 4 had the latest-only interruption gap. Revision 5 adds the same gap for absent stages.

#### Medium — adjustment

**FPROTO-5-05 — Prove browser binding on an effective body, including revalidation.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:401–404,427–431,501–505,574–583`.

Origin, path and decoded digest are the right binding for an observed envelope. No planned
browser control substitutes different bytes at the canonical package URL. The corrupt-envelope
control stops at assembly, and the CDN control checks a different exemption. A collector that
skips package bodies by URL would therefore pass those controls. The bodyless `304` example also
needs to distinguish the wire reply from the effective response. CDP can report a wire `304`
alongside effective `200` with reused content, as §2.7 already accounts for in the byte metric.
This is a validation gap supported by the protocol, with no candidate trace in this review.
[CDP Network domain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-protocol/master/pdl/domains/Network.pdl), [RFC 9111 §4.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html#section-4.3.3).

Require capture of the effective bytes or a traceable binding to the same previously inspected
representation on cache reuse. A missing effective body is inconclusive. Test the clean envelope,
a single clear body at its URL with the inspector's own diagnosis, and a warm revalidation without
proven body identity. Revision 1 recorded requests. Revision 2 added body collection without
package binding. The digest rule and explicit bodyless-status exception arrived in revision 5.

**FPROTO-5-06 — The G mutation changes the assembly input and the detail rows.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:123–127,213–221,519–537`.

The separate shape check admits G's 12 added rows. Assembly still says the opened rows must equal
the drawn fixture, which lacks them. Even with successful assembly, the canonical detail under
`todos` or `fixture_canal_c` in month five is missing 12 rows the mutant legitimately renders.
The scratch DuckDB query reproduced those differences and confirmed that only G's summary cell
changes. The general instruction to retain the canonical expectation and fail only on G leaves
these two comparisons at odds with the control.

Pass the derived rows as this control's expected package input. Check its detail against those
rows and retain the canonical expectation specifically for G's summary cell. Require a successful
open, a clean mutant detail comparison and the specific G refusal. The live G mutant dates to
revision 2. The current assembly row identity requirement and the G-only assertion are in revision 5.

**FPROTO-5-07 — The five warm samples can start from different cache states.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:566–589,716–717`.

Closing each tab and waiting for quiescence ends in-flight work. It leaves a single profile for
all five samples after one prime. Chrome can create a disk code-cache entry on a second use of an
eligible script and consume it on the third, saving compilation time. That change can happen with
the same HTTP cache hit flags and no live target from the preceding sample. The warm median can
mix first-warm and later code-cache states. This is an inference from Chrome's documented cache
lifecycle and the sampling schedule. [V8 code-cache lifecycle](https://v8.dev/blog/code-caching-for-devs#code-caching-recap).

Start each warm sample after the same predeclared priming sequence from independent profiles,
or report distinct start states separately. Check the priming and sample traces against the
same artifact and delivery condition. Revision 1 mixed cold and warm samples. Revision 2
introduced the separate warm statistic over a progressively reused profile, which remains here.

**FPROTO-5-08 — The per-candidate targets leave the shared draw implicit.**
`docs/framework_prototype.md:152–156,698–701,731–741`.

§7 correctly puts A6 and A1 in the clear-mode phase, then A7, A2 and A3 before one draw against
both encrypted builds. §5 also gives each `make prototype-*` target its own build, draw and
assembly. The target contract leaves unstated how the first invocation obtains both archived
outputs, or how a later rebuild of one candidate invalidates both packages and measurements.
Independent invocations can produce different fixtures and timings even though §6 reports one
comparison. The conflict is static. The per-candidate targets date to revision 1. The shared
post-build draw was added in revision 3, while the target descriptions retained a draw each.

Give the entry points one shared source for the pair of final builder digests and the draw.
Exercise the first invocation and a rerun of either candidate. Comparison requires both artifacts
to carry the same package digest. A rebuild invalidates both sets of measurements, and an
infeasible candidate leaves the comparison explicitly incomplete.

### 6. Limitations and open questions

- `PLAN.md:141` and the prototype plan's §1, §5, §8 and §9 agree on N95. Deliberately deceptive
  page code or a compromised dependency bypassing the observed reader is a residual-risk
  observation, because it requires code acting against the oracle. The findings above concern
  ordinary operations, the unchanged reader or requirements for the harness itself.
- Full wrapper and cache seeding, A1–A7, target attachment in the installed Chrome, control
  diagnoses on actual artifacts, collision rate and all comparison measurements remain pending.
  M54 and the earlier sandbox and WASM outputs are dated evidence. Revision 5 still marks the
  prototype results as pending. PLAN §7 leaves the framework decision to the Owner.
